nom: La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Serum Dark Spot Corrector

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin report the serum absorbs quickly without leaving an oily or greasy residue, with one noting it also has a purifying, clarifying effect suited to oily or acne-prone skin.
segments.dry: One reviewer with combo/dry skin found it effective for dark spots, though another reviewer generally warns the serum can dry the skin out if not paired with moisturizer.
segments.combination: Reviewers describing combination or combo/dry skin report the serum cleared their complexion and faded dark spots without complaints of irritation.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin are split: several report no burning, irritation, or breakouts and good results on discoloration, while one with generally sensitive skin had facial irritation after a single use and one skipped nighttime use due to redness and itching from product transferring to skin.
segments.mature: One 58-year-old reviewer in menopause and one 59-year-old reviewer both report the serum improved post-acne darkening and uneven tone despite hormone-related flare-ups.

concerns.aging: One reviewer mentions an age spot that lightened dramatically, though this same case turned out to be melanoma rather than a true age spot, underscoring a caution rather than a cosmetic result.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers note the serum is lightweight and non-greasy with a moisturizing feel, but at least two explicitly warn it dried their skin out and recommend layering moisturizer on top.
concerns.redness: Most reviewers report no irritation or redness even with regular use, but a small number describe facial irritation, itching, or redness, in one case appearing after just one application.
concerns.barrier: Reviewers largely report the serum did not compromise their skin, describing it as gentle, soothing, and non-stinging, with no mentions of barrier damage.
concerns.spots: The large majority of reviewers report visible fading of dark spots, sun spots, or melasma within one to several weeks of consistent use; however, several reviewers used it for weeks to months (one for a full bottle) with no visible change at all, and one notes it worked better as a spot treatment than all over the face.
concerns.blemishes: Many reviewers report the serum faded post-acne marks and acne scars, sometimes within one to three weeks; one reviewer reports it did not help with a specific sunspot despite following directions.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily-leaning skin report the serum does not add oiliness and absorbs without a greasy residue, with no reports of increased oiliness from use.

aspects.libelle: Can be drying without added moisturizer

extraits.titre: Did Little or Nothing for My Dark Spots
extraits.texte: When I saw that this serum had ten percent Niacinamide (most have only four), I had high hopes for it. I have a couple of darkened patches on my left cheek and some visible spots on the right side of my forehead. I used the serum consistently every night (may have missed a night or two, but was very regular in application) for about two months. I used up the entire bottle and saw no difference in my dark spots at all. VERY disappointed. Off to the dermatologist I go, hoping an RX product can finally do the job.

extraits.titre: Not a fan of the product scent
extraits.texte: I'm a La Roche-Posay fan, so when this dropped, I was intrigued to try it as I am struggling with discoloration/post-acne spots. The dry down feeling on the skin is comparable to their Toleriane Double Repair Matte Face Moisturizer if you've had the opportunity to try that. This is definitely oily skin friendly. The only thing I did not like is the scent of the product. Upon first putting it on, I thought it smelled a bit grape, but it quickly turned into that medical office type smell. It was just too scented for my liking. I did see some evening of my skin tone while using it, but unfortunately couldn't stay the course. If scented products aren't bothersome to you, it's worth trying.

I'm a 58 yr old black woman in menopause. My oily skin and hormone changes has activated acne and darkening on my cheeks. Acne medication, no help. Skin lightener only made me break out more. Then about a week ago a clip on TicTok had a quick reference and pic for what to use for different skin issues. From that I was introduced to niacinamide. I immediately went to Ulta. Wasn't sure what brand to try but this was the first I found so I bought it. Less than 2 weeks of using this twice a day, I already see a significant lightening in my darkest area.

My dermatologist gave me some samples of this serum for my face because I had dark spots and I literally swear by this! I did see results within the 4 weeks and still continue to use it since I have a couple of other spots around my forehead and jawline. My skin is more of a combo/dry. It's def on the more expensive side but this is really the only product that has worked for my dark spots. Personally, I don't mind the scent as it is not very strong and I like it, but if you're sensitive to scents, I'd be wary. The texture is NOT watery, nor is it sticky or oily, but it is slightly more thicker than watery. However, it does absorb nicely into the skin when I rub it in, doesn't pill with other skin products I use, and my skin doesn't feel sticky at all. Honestly, I feel like I'm getting closer to getting the glass skin I want lol. I would highly HIGHLY recommend this to anyone wanting to get rid of dark spots < 3

This improved my rosacea more than my melasma which is why I'm on my 3rd bottle. I am just now starting to see improvement with melasma but my rosacea improved immediately. It's so soothing on the skin and I've been getting compliments on how my skin glows. My skin is smoother and softer. Love this stuff! I use after toner and before moisturizer (and SPF in the daytime and retinol at night).
I have sensitive, acne-prone skin and this fades my acne scars and evened out my tone without burning or irritating my skin or breaking me out. In the morning my skin feels smooth and plump.

extraits.titre: Not sure if would but again
extraits.texte: I'm not sure about this product yet as I have only been using for about a week. I can't use it at night because it gets on my pillow and then on my neck and causes irritation, itching and redness. So I'm just using it during the day. Haven't noticed any difference yet.
